title: Does pairwise adjacency imply a simplex in the permutation-triangular K-theory complex?
statement: For a nonzero unital ring \(A\), let the vertices be stable invertible matrices, and let a finite set be a simplex when it lies in one left coset of a subgroup of matrices unitriangular for one permutation of the coordinate order. Must every finite pairwise adjacent set be a simplex? The notebook first asks the three-vertex case and then the finite version.
status: As of 9 November 2026, the literal assertion is false. It was explicitly asserted in \citet[\S11, Remark~(c)]{vaserstein1976foundations}, not left undisclosed. The appendix gives a complete proof for the triple \(I+E_{12},I+E_{23},I+E_{31}\) over every nonzero unital ring, checks invariance under stabilization and coset conventions, and includes independent exact computation. This is a correction of a published claim, with no assertion of priority for the counterexample.

title: Homogeneous additive cocycles and formal-law indecomposables
statement: For each \(n\ge2\) and commutative ring \(K\), determine normalized homogeneous polynomials \(h(x,y)\) satisfying \(h(x,y)+h(x+y,z)=h(y,z)+h(x,y+z)\), and distinguish the symmetric solutions from the unrestricted ones. The formal-law indecomposable calculation concerns the symmetric part.
status: As of November 2026: the symmetric classification is established by \citet[\S~II, Lemma~3]{lazard1955formal}, circulated December 1954 and published 1955. It is freely parametrized by the primitive integral binomial cocycle in each degree. The notebook's temporary nonsymmetric cubic example is corrected in 1972-276.14; its extra parameter is two-torsion, not three-torsion. These are expository occurrences, not an unsolved 1972 conjecture.

title: Determine the smooth normal-invariant homotopy groups
statement: Under the reconstructed interpretation of the notebook's \(K_J\) as stable bundles with a specified spherical trivialization, determine \(\pi_q(G/O)\) in all degrees, including the extensions in the homotopy exact sequence of \(G/O\to BO\to BG\). No finite range is specified in the notes.
status: As of November 2026: partially developed. The exact-sequence reduction and many finite ranges are established; no complete all-degree numerical determination was located in the primary sources checked. \citet[\S~9.2]{ranicki2002surgery} gives the normal-invariant framework. \citet[Theorem~1.1]{burklundisaksenxu2026synthetic}, first circulated 2 August 2024, online 2025, volume 2026, illustrates continued finite stable-stem progress. This does not itself compute all groups \(\pi_q(G/O)\). The source sentence is programmatic, and the identification has medium confidence.

title: Homotopy structures and the obstruction to surgery
statement: For a closed simply connected smooth \(n\)-manifold \(M\), \(n\ge6\), describe its marked homotopy structure set and determine when a degree-one normal map is normally bordant to a homotopy equivalence. These dimensional and compactness hypotheses reconstruct the range intended by the surgery continuation.
status: As of November 2026: the structural question was solved before these lectures. The surgery exact sequence identifies the image of the normal-invariant map with the zero fibre of the \(L_n(\mathbb Z)\)-valued obstruction. See \citet[Theorem~3]{sullivan1996triangulating}, circulated 1967, and the precise action-sequence formulation in \citet[Theorem~13.2]{ranicki2002surgery}. The source gives no particular manifold whose numerical structure set is left to compute.

title: Uniqueness of transverse normal maps and the left surgery term
statement: For a fixed smooth normal invariant over a closed simply connected manifold of dimension at least six, determine the ambiguity of transverse Pontryagin--Thom representatives, and decide when a normal bordism between homotopy-equivalence representatives can be changed relative to its ends to an h-cobordism.
status: As of November 2026: resolved structurally by normal bordism and relative surgery. A normal invariant specifies a normal-bordism class; the \(L_{n+1}(\mathbb Z)\) action accounts for the ambiguity of homotopy structures in a fibre, and the relative surgery obstruction tests a chosen bordism. See \citet[Propositions~9.43, 9.48 and Theorem~13.2]{ranicki2002surgery}; the pre-lecture sequence is in \citet[Theorem~3]{sullivan1996triangulating}. The compressed notebook attribution to Milnor--Kervaire or Novikov's dissertation was not matched to a unique proposition.

title: Classification of finite-type quivers
statement: For which finite connected quivers are there only finitely many indecomposable finite-dimensional representations up to isomorphism?
status: As of 9 November 2026: Solved before the talks by Gabriel 1972; ADE is the exact list. The 1973 BGP proof is an exact subsequent exposition.

title: The tame infinite boundary for quivers
statement: Which connected quivers of infinite representation type avoid the arbitrary-matrix-pair classification problem?
status: As of 9 November 2026: Solved: extended Dynkin type, with standard affine limiting cases. Nazarova’s exact paper was received 19 September 1972 before these talks and published 1973.

title: Completeness and coefficients of the one-sided Kostyuchenko system
statement: For real \(\gamma\), determine completeness, minimality and coefficient functionals for \(\{e^{\gamma nx}\sin nx:n\ge1\}\) in \(L^2(0,\pi)\), and distinguish completeness from the basis property.
status: As of 9 November 2026: Completeness was proved by Levin 1971, before the seminar, according to the later primary papers. The system is minimal; for nonzero real \(\gamma\) it is not a Schauder basis, whereas \(\gamma=0\) is the sine basis. The signed system in the notebook is redundant and must not be substituted for this precise problem. The asserted particular Schwarz--Christoffel formula was not verified.

title: The Adams conjecture for stable spherical fibrations
statement: For every finite CW-complex X, integer \(k\ge2\), and virtual real bundle \(x\in KO(X)\), does some \(k^N\) annihilate \(J(\psi^k x-x)\)?
status: As of 9 November 2026: proved before the seminar: Sullivan’s June 1970 notes, Corollary 5.9, and Quillen’s 1971 Theorem 1.1 (received 3 July 1970). The notebook’s separate reverse formula is false and is not this conjecture.

title: Off-diagonal zeros of the Bergman kernel
statement: For a bounded domain G the off-diagonal Bergman kernel can vanish. Every planar annulus \(r<|z|<1\), \(0<r<1\), has zeros. In contrast the disk and bounded homogeneous complete circular domains have zero-free kernels. Positivity of \(K(z,\bar z)\) on the diagonal is a different assertion.
status: As of 9 November 2026: The unrestricted question had a negative answer before this seminar. No broader classification problem is silently substituted.

title: Ordinary p-adic interpolation of modular L-values
statement:
Let \(\chi\) be a nontrivial primitive even character of conductor \(q=p^r\), with its values embedded in a finite p-adic extension. Use the preceding measure for the even component
     \(P(x)=(I(x)+I(-x))/(2\Omega_+)\), \(I(x)=\int_x^{i\infty}f(z)dz\), normalized algebraically. Then
     \[\int_{\mathbb Z_p^\times}\chi^{-1}\,d\mu_\alpha=\alpha^{-r}\sum_{a\bmod q}\chi^{-1}(a)P(a/q).\]
     With \(\tau(\chi^{-1})=\sum_a\chi^{-1}(a)e^{2\pi ia/q}\), the sum is the algebraic value represented over the complex numbers by \(i\tau(\chi^{-1})L(f,\chi,1)/(2\pi\Omega_+)\). The complex expression is transported p-adically through its algebraic normalization, not by embedding arbitrary complex periods.
status: As of 9 November 2026: Resolved by the 1973 construction under the precise ordinary and period hypotheses; this is the definite question tracked in the problem index.
